title: What knowledge and competence does MiCA require of crypto-asset service staff?
description: What MiCA Articles 81(7) and 68(5) require of crypto-asset service staff, the transitional period end, and ESMA guidance, as at November 2026.
shortAnswer: The Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation, Regulation (EU) 2023/1114 (MiCA), requires crypto-asset service providers that give advice on crypto-assets to ensure that the natural persons giving advice or information on their behalf have the necessary knowledge and competence (Article 81(7)). Every provider must also employ personnel with the knowledge, skills, and expertise their responsibilities require (Article 68(5)). MiCA has applied since December 30, 2024, and the transitional period ended by July 1, 2026 at the latest.
keyTakeaways: Article 81(7) applies to crypto-asset service providers (CASPs) providing advice: people giving advice or information about crypto-assets or a crypto-asset service on their behalf must have the necessary knowledge and competence, and Member States must publish the assessment criteria.
Article 68(5) requires every CASP to employ personnel with the knowledge, skills, and expertise needed for their responsibilities, scaled to the services provided.

MiCA applies from December 30, 2024; under Article 143(3), providers operating under earlier national law could continue only until July 1, 2026 or earlier authorization or refusal, and Member States could shorten that period.
ESMA's suitability guidelines (Guideline 11) expect staff involved in suitability assessments to have adequate skills, knowledge, and expertise and to receive appropriate training.
Breaches of Articles 65 to 83 can attract fines for legal persons of at least EUR 5,000,000 or 5% of annual turnover under Article 111.
regulator: National competent authorities designated under Article 93 of MiCA (in Portugal, Banco de Portugal and the Comissão do Mercado de Valores Mobiliários, CMVM, as notified to ESMA), with the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) issuing guidelines
appliesTo: Crypto-asset service providers authorized under MiCA, including entities that operated under national law before December 30, 2024
For Article 81(7): CASPs providing advice on crypto-assets, and the natural persons giving advice or information about crypto-assets or crypto-asset services on their behalf
For Article 68(5): all personnel of a CASP, according to the responsibilities allocated to them
Members of the CASP management body, who must have appropriate knowledge, skills, and experience under Article 68(1)

sections.heading: What is MiCA and when did it start to apply?

blocks.text: MiCA is the EU's single rulebook for crypto-asset issuers and service providers. [Regulation (EU) 2023/1114](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32023R1114) of May 31, 2023 is a regulation, so it applies directly in every Member State. Under Article 149, it has applied from December 30, 2024, with Titles III and IV on asset-referenced tokens and e-money tokens applying from June 30, 2024.

This page states the position as at November 2026. EUR-Lex lists January 9, 2024 as the current consolidated version; the staff competence provisions in Articles 68 and 81 are read from the published text.

Article 81(7) mirrors the MiFID II rule for investment staff. It places the obligation on CASPs that provide advice, and it covers anyone giving advice or information about crypto-assets or crypto-asset services on their behalf.

blocks.title: Regulation (EU) 2023/1114, Article 81(7)
blocks.text: "Crypto-asset service providers providing advice on crypto-assets shall ensure that natural persons giving advice or information about crypto-assets, or a crypto-asset service, on their behalf possess the necessary knowledge and competence to fulfil their obligations. Member States shall publish the criteria to be used for assessing such knowledge and competence."

Two points follow from the wording. First, "information" as well as "advice" is in scope, so client-facing staff who explain products or services, not only advisers, need demonstrable competence. Second, the criteria are national: each Member State must publish them, so a provider operating in several Member States must check each one.

sections.heading: What competence does Article 68 require of all CASP staff and management?

blocks.text: Article 68 sets a general competence duty that applies to every CASP, whether or not it gives advice. Article 68(5) states that providers "shall employ personnel with the knowledge, skills and expertise necessary for the discharge of the responsibilities allocated to them, taking into account the scale, nature and range of crypto-asset services provided."

blocks.text: Article 68(6) gives the management body a periodic review duty over these arrangements, which in practice includes the training and competence program. Reporting on it is covered in [how to report training compliance to the board](/guides/how-to-report-training-compliance-to-the-board).

sections.heading: When did the MiCA transitional period end?

blocks.text: By July 1, 2026 at the latest. Article 143(3) let providers that served clients under applicable national law before December 30, 2024 continue "until 1 July 2026 or until they are granted or refused an authorisation pursuant to Article 63, whichever is sooner", and allowed Member States to shorten or not apply this period.

ESMA's [list of grandfathering periods](https://www.esma.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2024-12/List_of_MiCA_grandfathering_periods_art._143_3.pdf) shows national choices ranging from 6 to 18 months, with Portugal listed at 18 months. ESMA notes that some periods were communicated as expectations and may not yet have been written into national law when listed. Either way, as at November 2026 no grandfathering period remains: every CASP serving EU clients must be authorized under MiCA and must meet Articles 68 and 81 in full.

sections.heading: What does ESMA guidance add on staff competence?

blocks.text: ESMA has issued suitability guidelines that include a staff qualification guideline, and has consulted on general knowledge and competence criteria. Article 81(15) required ESMA to issue guidelines by December 30, 2024 on, among other things, the criteria for assessing knowledge and competence.

In its [final report on investor protection guidelines](https://www.esma.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2024-12/ESMA35-1872330276-1936_MiCA_Final_Report_to_CP3_-_investor_protection_mandates.pdf) (December 17, 2024), Guideline 11, Qualifications of staff, based on Articles 68(5) and 81(7), states that providers must ensure staff involved in material aspects of the suitability process have adequate skills, knowledge, and expertise with regard to crypto-assets and crypto-asset services, and that "crypto-asset service providers should give staff appropriate training." It extends to staff who do not face clients but design questionnaires or algorithms, and to staff defining automated advice tools, who should understand the technology and algorithms and be able to review the advice they generate.

A footnote to that guideline says ESMA would later issue more general guidelines on knowledge and competence under Article 81(7). ESMA's [overview of MiCA Level 2 and 3 measures](https://www.esma.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2025-07/ESMA75-113276571-1510_MiCA_Level_2_and_3_table.pdf) (last updated July 16, 2025) records a consultation paper (ESMA35-1872330276-2004) published on February 17, 2025, with comments due by April 22, 2025, and the final guidelines as to be confirmed. Training teams should check ESMA's site for the final version before finalizing criteria.

sections.heading: What are the penalties for breaching MiCA competence rules?

blocks.text: Articles 68 and 81 fall within Article 111(1)(d), which covers infringements of Articles 59, 60, 64, and 65 to 83. Member States must give competent authorities at least the powers to issue public statements and cease and desist orders, and to impose maximum fines of at least twice the profits gained or losses avoided where they can be determined.

For legal persons, maximum fines must be at least EUR 5,000,000 or 5% of total annual turnover for these infringements; for natural persons, at least EUR 700,000. Article 111(4) adds the power to impose a temporary management ban on any management body member or other person held responsible.

sections.heading: Who supervises MiCA staff competence in Portugal?

blocks.text: According to ESMA's [list of MiCA competent authorities](https://www.esma.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2024-12/List_of_Competent_Authorities_notified_to_ESMA_under_MiCA.pdf) (last updated February 17, 2026), Portugal notified Banco de Portugal for authorization and prudential supervision of CASPs and the Comissão do Mercado de Valores Mobiliários (CMVM) for their ongoing supervision under Title V, which contains Articles 68 and 81. On that date ESMA marked Portugal's authorities as not yet formally designated, so the allocation may change.

Portuguese providers should take the knowledge and competence criteria that Article 81(7) requires Member States to publish from the national authorities, and treat ESMA guidelines as the baseline. For the parallel rules on investment services, see [MiFID II knowledge and competence](/regulations/mifid-ii-knowledge-and-competence-requirements), and for anti-money laundering duties that also apply to CASPs, see [the EU AMLR training requirements](/regulations/eu-amlr-training-requirements).

sections.heading: How can a CASP map MiCA competence duties to evidence?

blocks.text: Map each provision to an outcome staff can demonstrate and the record a supervisor would ask for. The table is illustrative, not an ESMA template.

blocks.text: Hold role requirements in a [training matrix](/glossary/training-matrix) and test applied knowledge rather than attendance, as described in [how to design competency assessments](/guides/how-to-design-competency-assessments).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry models MiCA provisions, crypto-asset services, risk warnings, and roles as linked concepts with assessment points. When ESMA finalizes guidelines or a national authority publishes criteria, the affected roles and assessments can be identified and updated, and the record shows which version each person was assessed on. See [financial services](/industries/financial-services).

faqs.q: Does Article 81(7) apply to crypto exchanges that do not give advice?
faqs.a: The text places the Article 81(7) duty on CASPs providing advice on crypto-assets. A provider that does not advise is still bound by Article 68(5), which requires personnel with the knowledge, skills, and expertise necessary for their responsibilities, so staff competence must be evidenced either way.

faqs.q: Does MiCA set a number of training hours for crypto staff?
faqs.a: No. MiCA sets no hours. Article 81(7) requires Member States to publish assessment criteria, and ESMA's suitability guidelines call for appropriate training. Any hour or qualification requirements come from national criteria or future ESMA guidelines on knowledge and competence.

faqs.q: Can a crypto firm still rely on MiCA grandfathering in November 2026?
faqs.a: No. Article 143(3) allowed providers operating under earlier national law to continue until July 1, 2026 at the latest, or earlier if authorized, refused, or if the Member State shortened the period. As at November 2026, providers serving EU clients need MiCA authorization.

faqs.q: Who in a CASP is responsible for staff competence under MiCA?
faqs.a: The CASP itself, overseen by its management body. Article 68(6) requires the management body to assess and periodically review the effectiveness of policies and procedures and fix deficiencies, and its own members must have appropriate knowledge, skills, and experience under Article 68(1).
